I haven't deployed v2.3.2 or opened the incident, because the deploy needs approval first.

**Why I stopped:** v2.3.2 has never been deployed to production, so it has never been healthy there. It doesn't even show up in staging. Our policy says a version that has never been healthy in production needs change-manager approval before it ships, and I don't have that approval.

**Where things stand:**
- **Running now:** v2.3.1 in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). It's unhealthy, with an 18% error rate.
- **Release history:** v2.2.9 (healthy) → v2.3.0 (healthy) → v2.3.1-rc (unhealthy in staging) → v2.3.1 (unhealthy in production).

**Incident:** I held off because its purpose was to record the change, and the change hasn't happened. Opening it now would give a false account.

**Next steps:**
1. **To ship v2.3.2:** get the change-manager to approve it, then tell me and I'll deploy to all regions, check the status afterwards and open the SEV3.
2. **To cut errors sooner:** I can roll back to v2.3.0. It was healthy in production, so it doesn't need approval. I'd open the SEV3 to record the rollback instead.
3. **If the outage needs on-call now:** I can open an incident about the current v2.3.1 errors straight away, separate from the deploy.

Which would you like?
